eras.name: the Burn
eras.summary: launch and the boost; 72,000 voyagers in nine Charter Towns; the Charter; the first children; the Burn Fever
eras.governance: the Captain-Governor, the Wardens and the first Assembly
eras.tech: full: the Wardens run the ship beside the Steward

eras.name: the Filling

eras.governance: the Assembly and Moderator; the Wardens

eras.name: the Settled Age
eras.summary: the Balance holds; the churches unite and settle; the College; the Heritage Revival fixes the Great Lakes ways; the Last Snow; Earth's Letters read aloud on Sundays
eras.governance: the Assembly; the Wardens as a learned corps
eras.tech: full, but fewer people learn it

eras.name: the Troubles

eras.tech: lost: the Lockout shuts people out of the machinery

eras.name: the Long Calm
eras.summary: a hundred quiet years: towns, churches, canneries, spinball and the great families; the Draw; the Earth-link falls silent; the Steward's Gift of the Air
eras.governance: the Assembly; town councils; the Marshals
eras.tech: use without understanding: the Chutes, pods and vans, aerostats

eras.name: the Present Age (living memory)
eras.summary: the Kettle Flood, the Gray Fever, the Share Scandal, the cannery closures and the Solana boom, the Bellhaven Dig, the Wire, the Waymakers, the Sunline Flicker, the Quincentennial and the Notice
eras.governance: the Assembly (Moderator Rosalind Achterberg-Nunez since VY 496)

future_eras.name: the Waking

future_eras.name: the Second Opening

future_eras.name: the Midpoint
future_eras.summary: halfway: the Midpoint Festival; slow change; a second Troubles over the shares (VY 910s)

future_eras.name: the Seeing
future_eras.summary: the destination star is shown on the Boards, brightening year by year; preparation

future_eras.name: the Long Brake
future_eras.summary: the drive wakes; thirty years of braking; the seas lean a hair to the south

future_eras.name: Arrival
future_eras.summary: Columbia reaches Alpha Centauri A and orbits Hesper; surveys

future_eras.name: the Divide
future_eras.summary: Planetfall; those who go down and those who stay; the station becomes 'the Old Country'

future_eras.name: the Old Country
future_eras.summary: the station as a heritage world in orbit, its population slowly falling

events.summary: the Hot Century: heat, drought, storms and rising seas reshape where people can live
detail: the American South and Southwest, the Gulf and Atlantic coasts and much of Mexico and the Caribbean become hard to live in
fresh water becomes the continent's measure of wealth
popular_version: a Sunday-school story of a flood of fire

events.summary: the Refuge: tens of millions move to the Great Lakes basin, the continent's cool, water-rich heart
detail: from Texas, Florida, Arizona, Louisiana, the Carolinas, Georgia, California, from Mexico, Puerto Rico, Cuba, Haiti, the Dominican Republic and Central America, and from Canada's burning west
Toledo, Cleveland, Detroit, Chicago, Buffalo, Milwaukee, Erie and Windsor double and double again
the southern Great Lakes become the most diverse region on the continent; the old Great Lakes ways (the fish fry, euchre, the parish festival, polka and the Friday night game) become everyone's
popular_version: 'everyone came to the Lakes, then the Lakes came here'

events.summary: the Lakes megaregion: the continent's industrial and scientific centre (fusion, space industry)
detail: fusion power stations along the lake shores
shipyards turn to spacecraft; Cleveland, Toledo and Detroit build for the Moon

events.summary: lunar mining and orbital yards make large ships possible
detail: the L2 yards
asteroid ice and metals

events.summary: the Hesperus interferometer finds oxygen on a planet of Alpha Centauri A: Hesper
detail: 0.92 Earth masses, 1.23 AU, oceans
the find electrifies the continent

events.summary: the North American Interstellar Compact founded at Toledo to build an ark for Hesper
detail: the US, Canada and Mexico, the Great Lakes states and provinces, companies and churches
Dr. Ingrid Kessler its first director-general
motive: 'a second home for the continent' (the Second Home movement), insurance against the Hot Century's return, and the pull of Hesper

events.summary: the Columbia design fixed: one cylinder, seas at the ends, a Sunline, and towns patterned on the Great Lakes' own
detail: the Heritage Mandate: towns built to the plans of real historic buildings from the Library of Congress archive (the pattern buildings), so the voyagers would live in familiar streets
European engineers (the ESA drive team under Henrik Aaltonen) design the drive and the rotation bearings
popular_version: people think the old buildings were 'brought from Earth'

events.summary: construction at the L2 yard
detail: 37 years; 11,000 builders; 212 deaths in yard accidents
popular_version: 'it took a hundred years to build'

events.summary: the ark Harmonia (European Union) launched for Tau Ceti
detail: contact lost 2279 (VY 27)
popular_version: sailors' ghost stories of a ship 'following ours'

events.summary: the Habitat Autonomy System (the Steward) commissioned to run the ship for three thousand years
detail: designed so that the voyagers need never understand the machinery
a three-thousand-year service life written into its core (the Long Clause)

events.summary: the Selection: 72,000 voyagers chosen from 4.1 million applicants in the Lakes megaregion
detail: half by lottery, half by trade (the Trades list: farmers, fishers, builders, teachers, nurses, doctors, engineers, cooks, musicians, clergy)
families went together; the genetic survey ensured diversity; a frozen bank of 1.2 million embryos and gametes (the Ark Bank) went too
popular_version: 'Grandmother X was a cook on the Trades list'

events.summary: the ark Tianhe (China) launched for Epsilon Eridani
detail: reported healthy in the Last Letter era

events.summary: the Goodbyes: the voyagers leave their homes and families; ferried up to the yard over eight months
detail: most left parents, siblings and friends behind forever
the last ferry left Toledo Port on 30 March 2252
popular_version: the custom of leaving an empty chair at Launch Day dinner

events.summary: the Charter of Columbia signed by the 72,000 on Launch Day
detail: the Charter Stone in Port Carrow bears the first 400 signatures
popular_version: the Charter is read aloud on Charter Day (4 July, moved from the US holiday)

events.summary: Tamsin Okafor-Reyes, the first child born aboard (12 June 2252, Port Carrow)
detail: the lake was named for her in VY 9
her name became one of the station's most beloved
popular_version: 'Tamsin was born as the Sun was lit' (she was born seven weeks later)
mothers pray to 'Saint Tamsin' (she was not a saint)

events.summary: Launch Day: Columbia leaves the L2 yard with 72,000 voyagers (21 April 2252)
detail: the Sunline lit at 06:00 ship time; the drive lit at 09:14
Captain-Governor Ada Carrow's words: 'We are the Lakes, carried'
popular_version: every family claims an ancestor at the launch window
children think the ship was launched from a lake

events.summary: the Letters: families on Earth write to the voyagers; replies take weeks, then months
the first Assembly sits in Kessler; Ada Carrow chosen first Moderator
Marcus Harrow drowns freeing the jammed Falls sluice; the town of Falls Landing renamed Harrow Falls
detail: his crew of six lived
popular_version: 'Harrow held back the whole river with his hands'

events.summary: the ark Kaveri (India and the Gulf states) launched for Alpha Centauri B
detail: will arrive after Columbia; the Letters mention it until 2410
popular_version: 'the ship behind us' (a Waymaker belief: the Kaveri follows Columbia)

events.summary: Tern Harbor founded by North Shore fishing families
the Burn Fever: a respiratory fever kills 2,900 over three years
detail: Dr. Esperanza Villalobos found the treatment in the Wardens' labs
whole families lost; the first mass Returns (funerals)
popular_version: 'the Fever came from Earth in a letter' (a myth)
Villalobos is a saint to South Shore Catholics

events.summary: Victory Bay founded and named for the end of the Burn Fever
the boost ends: the drive falls quiet and Columbia coasts (Coasting Day, 3 March 2283)
detail: no one felt it; the Wardens rang the Launch Bell 31 times
popular_version: 'the day the ship started to glide'

events.summary: Solana Point founded on the South Shore by families led by Rosario Solano and Tomás Reyes
detail: the first town not built by the Compact: raised from the Chutes' stock by its own people
popular_version: 'Solano and Reyes built the Point with their bare hands'

events.summary: the ark Pampa (the South American League) launched for 82 Eridani
the Turning: the station-born outnumber the Earth-born
Playa Verde founded by Spanish-speaking families from Solana Point
Pelican Cove founded as a fishing and canning village; pelicans released from the Ark Bank (they died out by VY 90)
Tamarack founded by dairy farmers, among them the Plain families
Brightwater founded as a pleasure town; its boardwalk the station's first
the Charter revision of VY 60 adopts the Voyage Year
Oceanview founded as a resort
spinball invented by schoolteacher Otis Merriweather in Harrow Falls: baseball remade for a world where thrown balls curve
detail: the diamond is turned spinward; the curve is part of the game

events.summary: the last people on Earth who knew a voyager die; the Letters become official news bulletins
the first Bank Children: births from the Ark Bank's embryos widen the station's gene pool
detail: about 9,000 over 48 years; 'Bank' is not an insult, though it was used as one
popular_version: 'Bank-born' families are said to be lucky

events.summary: Haven Point founded at the mouth of Lost Creek
Haskins Corner grows round the Haskins crossroads store
Port Tamsin founded on the north shore of Lake Tamsin
Dunmore Crossing grows at the Ring Line depot
Cedar Ford founded at the Kettle ford
the Balance Act: births licensed by shares as the station nears its means (Charter art. 7)
detail: one share each at 18; two to a child; gifting allowed within family (widened VY 440)
the Registry Office founded to keep the shares

events.summary: Loomis Grove planted as an orchard village
Wilhelmina 'Minnie' Kowalczyk, the Last Earthborn, dies at 110 in Fenwick (2359)
detail: born in Hamtramck in 2249, aboard at three
'I remember a sky with nothing in it' -- her famous line
popular_version: Minnie's Line is quoted at funerals

events.summary: Pruett hamlet named for surveyor Hollis Pruett
the Balance reached: 250,000 people (the Filling ends)
the Ring Line railway completed round the world
detail: 146 level crossings

events.summary: the Lakes Union Church formed from the station's Methodist, Lutheran, Presbyterian, Episcopal, Reformed and UCC congregations
the Wardens' College founded at Bellhaven (renamed Columbia College VY 290)
Rome (by the Earth-link) grants the Particular Church of Columbia its own rite and bishop; Bishop Casimir Nowicki
detail: priests may marry since VY 201 (the Columbian Indult)

events.summary: the Heritage Revival fixes the Great Lakes ways: the Friday fish fry, euchre leagues, the Northland Fair, Pączki Day, the polka Saturdays
detail: the Heritage Societies; Agnes Szabó's 'Book of the Lakes' (VY 184)
popular_version: people think these customs came unchanged from Earth

events.summary: the Fox Year: foxes released to curb the rabbits eat the chickens instead
popular_version: 'the Fox Year' is what you call any well-meant blunder

events.summary: the Station League of spinball founded; the first Spin Cup
the Last Snow (14 January 2464): after the Kettle Freeze, the Steward ends snowfall for the water balance
detail: snow is now remembered with paper-snow on Snow Night
popular_version: grandmothers' 'snow stories' are told as fairy tales

events.summary: the Green Message arrives: Earth is healed and invites the ark to consider returning
the Green Message: Earth reports the Hot Century's damage healed and invites the ark to consider return (a proposal, never an order)
detail: the trigger of the Returners movement and the Troubles
popular_version: 'there was no message; the Returners made it up'

events.summary: the Returners movement: 'turn Columbia home'
popular_version: Returners are villains in school plays

events.summary: the Referendum: 50.9% vote to ask the Steward to turn back; the Assembly petitions; the Steward does not answer
popular_version: 'we voted to go home and the machine said no'

events.summary: the Sternward March: 6,000 Returners walk to the South Sea wall to reach the Drive
the Marshals rule under emergency powers
the Stern Breach: Returner saboteurs blast an Undercroft hatch near the Drive; 61 die, the South Sea drops two metres
detail: Silas Brandvold among the dead; Warden Thaddeus Kowal sealed the breach and died of his burns
popular_version: 'the Returners tried to crash the ship'
Kowal is a hero; Brandvold a devil or a martyr, by family

events.summary: the Lockout: the Steward seals the Undercroft, the Port and the Drive; its Notice: THE UNDERCROFT IS CLOSED FOR THE SAFETY OF ALL
detail: no human has entered since, except the Chutes and the Return halls
the Wardens' skills wither within two generations (the Forgetting)
popular_version: 'the Steward locked the door because we were naughty'
children dare each other to knock on hatches

events.summary: the Wardens dissolved: with the machinery sealed, the technical corps has no work
the Gray Years: short rations as the Steward trims the Chutes; people learn to make do
the Reconciliation: amnesty, the Quiet Clause (Charter art. 21), the Returners disband; Moderator Josephine Adebayo-Ruiz
popular_version: 'the Quiet Clause means you mustn't talk about where we're going' (it doesn't)

events.summary: the Draw established: every household's food, home, air, water and clothing stock guaranteed
the Chutes begin issuing pods and vans: the electric cars of the Long Calm
the cannery boom at Tern Harbor and Pelican Cove
the Order of the Lamp founded in Port Carrow: lodge, charity, fish fries and funerals
the Port Carrow Mariners win eleven Spin Cups in fifteen years
St. Hedwig's Cathedral consecrated in Port Carrow
the Cannery and Dock Workers Union founded
the Last Letter from Earth; then only the Heartbeat
the Heartbeat: an automated pulse from Earth every 29 days; the Steward logs it; nobody reads it
popular_version: 'the Heartbeat means Earth is still there'

events.summary: the Last Letter: Earth's last message in plain language, strange in tone and hard to understand
detail: afterward only an automated pulse (the Heartbeat) every 29 days
Bellhaven scholars still argue what the Last Letter means

events.summary: the Gift of the Air: the Chutes release the first aerostats; the Steward's way of sending new things
popular_version: 'the Steward heard us wishing to fly'

events.summary: the Aerostat Pilots' Guild formed at Harrow Falls
the Assembly Hall in Kessler burns; the cause never found
detail: rebuilt by VY 425 to Ruth Abernathy-Chen's design

events.summary: the Forty Days: the Tern Harbor cannery strike, led by Declan Moriarty
popular_version: Moriarty is a hero on the North Shore, a troublemaker in Kessler

events.summary: the Spin Cup final riot, Mariners v. Suns, at the Sun Bowl
the first aerostat crash, Harrow Falls: three dead
the Gifting Act: shares may be gifted outside the family; Moderator Ignatius Bhatt
the Kettle Flood (the Deluge Week, 12-18 September 2699): the Steward's rain runs a week; the Kettle rises four metres; 214 dead at Cedar Ford and Dunmore Crossing
detail: Constable Marisol Ybarra-Quinn pulls 40 people from the water
the Flood Line painted on every building it reached
popular_version: 'the Steward was punishing the river towns'

events.summary: the Wire: the station network of radio and screens, founded by Leopold Varga-Hayes
aerostat racing begins at the Harrow Falls Aerodrome; Juniper Stroud the first champion
the Waymakers founded by Evangeline Mbeki-Hart: the voyage itself is the pilgrimage
detail: 'We are not lost. We are on the Way.'
popular_version: 'the only people who care where we're going'

events.summary: the Gray Fever: 4,100 die in eighteen months (October 2713 - spring 2715)
detail: nurse Anh Tran-Delacroix's clinic at Pelican Cove
the old and the very young hit hardest

events.summary: the Fever Children: an Assembly share bonus brings a birth bump
popular_version: the Fever Children (born VY 464-470, aged 30-36 now) are said to be lucky and pushy

events.summary: the Share Scandal: Moderator Harlan Duquesne's circle caught selling shares; he resigns; share sale made a crime
popular_version: 'every Kessler lawyer was in on it'

events.summary: Duquesne's trial: seven years; released VY 475; lives quietly in Oceanview
the Tern Harbor cannery closes (Castellanos-Pike Canning); 1,100 jobs
the Tern Exodus: families leave Tern Harbor for Solana Point
the Solana boom: Pier Plaza and Pacific City built by Luis 'Lucky' Arrieta-Wu
the Solana Point Suns win six Spin Cups (VY 476-488), led by Dante Okonkwo-Silva
the Delmar Cannery fire, Pelican Cove: nine dead; arson suspected, never solved
popular_version: 'the Delmars burned it for the insurance'

events.summary: the Bellhaven Dig: five students open a sealed Undercroft hatch; four come back; Imogen Sato-Ferris is never found
detail: the Steward resealed the hatch within the hour
the Wardens' Library circle revived
popular_version: 'she ran off to the Far Side'

events.summary: 'The Lamplighters' begins on the Wire: the most loved radio serial of the age
the Census Row: the Registry's count and the Steward's air figures disagree by 1,100 people ('the Missing Eleven Hundred')
popular_version: 'there are people living in the Undercroft'

events.summary: Obadiah Kincaid-Morales becomes the first Marshal-General from the Southland
the Long Session: seven months of Assembly deadlock over the Undercroft Inquiry Bill; Charter art. 23 (the right to petition the Steward) added
the Great Regatta on Lake Tamsin: 400 boats
the Brightwater Boardwalk rebuilt after the rot
Harrow Mill No. 2 closes; the Falls Pier opens the same summer
the Quincentennial Commission formed under Beatriz Holloway-Anand
Rosalind Achterberg-Nuñez (Charter League) chosen Moderator over Tobias Wainwright-Okafor (Open Hand), 52 to 49
the Registry Leak: share records read out on the Wire by Margit Kovács-Lee; who gifted to whom, and who didn't
popular_version: families feuding over what the Leak revealed

events.summary: the Sunline Flicker (17 August 2750): the Sunline dims for eleven minutes at noon; churches fill; the Steward says nothing
the Flicker Petition: the Assembly petitions the Steward under art. 23; no reply
the Port Carrow Mariners win their first Spin Cup in thirty years
the spring of VY 500: the Notice debated in the Assembly; Waymaker revival meetings; Charter Day and the Quincentennial Fair to come; the Midsummer Regatta
the Quincentennial Launch Day (21 April 2752): five hundred years; parades in every town, the Launch Bell rung 500 times
the Notice: at noon on Launch Day every public board reads VOYAGE ONE THIRD COMPLETE. ALL SYSTEMS WITHIN BALANCE. The Steward's first words since VY 271
detail: it stayed up for one day
the talk of the spring: what's the other two thirds? where are we going? who wrote it?
popular_version: 'we're a third of the way to Heaven' (Waymakers)

future_events.summary: the Steward answers a petition for the first time: a list of the station's systems and their condition
future_events.hook_for_present: the Notice suggests the Steward may speak

future_events.summary: the truth of Imogen Sato-Ferris (left for the story engine to decide; the bible reserves it)
the Second Opening: trained people allowed into the Undercroft; the Wardens re-founded
the Heartbeat decoded: Earth has been sending its history for two hundred years
the Midpoint (2 March 3002): the station's greatest festival
the second Troubles: the shares fought over; the Balance holds
the Boards begin showing the destination star
the ark Kaveri's signal detected, following
future_events.hook_for_present: the Waymaker belief in 'the ship behind us'

future_events.summary: the drive wakes for the Long Brake
arrival at Alpha Centauri A (21 April 3752); orbit round Hesper
Planetfall: the first 3,000 go down to Hesper
the Divide: the station votes to remain a home for those who stay
the last census at the Balance; the population falls after
the station called 'the Old Country' on Hesper; pilgrimages to Port Carrow
the Notice of the Long Clause: SERVICE LIFE ENDS IN FIFTY YEARS
